critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL — CypherReferencePanel.jsx:198 was passing prop name `ref` to a function component, which React reserves for forwardRef. The component received undefined and crashed the entire panel with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading tier_progression)'. The Atelier > References subtab was completely unusable for cypher campaigns until tester fixed it. Add an ESLint rule (`react/no-named-as-default-member` won't catch this; consider `react/forbid-component-props` with `ref` for non-forwardRef components, or a project-level grep ban).

XP-events ledger atomic semantics are correctly enforced server-side (peer-transfer is single-write, intrusion-grant pairs +2/-1 acceptor with +1 peer in one transaction). No client-side compensation logic needed.

rca of the issue: Single FE crash: CypherReferencePanel.jsx:198 called <RuleStrip ref={ref}/>. React treats `ref` on a function component (without forwardRef) as a special prop that is consumed by React itself and never forwarded to the child component's props bag. So inside RuleStrip the destructured `ref` was undefined, and the next line `(ref.tier_progression || []).map(...)` threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading tier_progression)' — surfaced via React error overlay 'Uncaught runtime errors:' that blanked the whole References subtab. Reproduction: log in as GMFran, navigate to any cypher campaign > Atelier > References. Expected: panel renders. Observed (pre-fix): error overlay with three stack traces all pointing at RuleStrip. Mitigation applied by tester: renamed prop `ref` → `data` at both call site (line 198) and definition (line 447), and added `const ref = data || {}` defensive normalisation inside RuleStrip so the rest of the component body can keep its existing variable name. After hot-reload: 0 console errors, 32 testids visible, all 6 sub-tabs interactive, cypher roll button returns a result card, bestiary loads. The component already had `ref.tier_progression || []` guards but they were powerless because `ref` itself was undefined — the bug was strictly the prop-name collision.
